items.note: Hamstring, week-to-week, officially out for tonight. Case Keenum (38, no meaningful action since 2023) CONFIRMED as starting QB per Yahoo/NBC Chicago/ABC7 gameday reporting -- Tyson Bagent remains in concussion protocol and will not play. This resolves the week-long Bagent-vs-Keenum uncertainty in the worse direction. Keeping at -6.5 (top of the QB-out range) given Keenum's extreme unfamiliarity with this offense and lack of recent reps.

analysis: Case Keenum is now CONFIRMED as the Bears' starter tonight (Yahoo, NBC Chicago, ABC7) -- Caleb Williams (hamstring) is out and Tyson Bagent remains in concussion protocol, so the week-long Bagent-vs-Keenum uncertainty resolved in the worse direction for Chicago: a 38-year-old third-stringer with no meaningful snaps since 2023 making his first start of the year. The injury-adjusted model still has Chicago at -6.5 pts on offense, and with raw Elo essentially a coinflip (+0.5 home) the model's -6.0 adjusted margin is now almost entirely the QB downgrade talking, not a team-strength read.

The market actually got MORE favorable for Eagles bettors late in the week, not less: the number peaked at Eagles -4.5 mid-week (Tue-Thu) and has since drifted back to -3/-3.5 into kickoff even as the QB news got worse for the Bears and 74-83% of bets and handle piled onto Philadelphia. That combination -- a real, newly-confirmed talent gap the market hasn't fully re-priced, plus a number that softened rather than hardened -- is what turns this from a marginal, market-matching spread lean into a real one. The total lean is the cleaner, higher-conviction side of the two: model total (40.1) sits well under the market's 44.5, and Keenum's unfamiliarity with this offense argues for a slower, lower-scoring Bears night on top of the raw injury math.

leans.reasoning: Injury-adjusted model total (40.1) sits well below the market total and Keenum's confirmed start (vs. Bagent, who at least had 2025 starter reps) only reinforces the downgrade.

Model margin (-6.0 adjusted) has pulled further ahead of the market number as the market drifted back toward Chicago late week (-4.5 mid-week to -3/-3.5 at kickoff) despite the QB news getting worse for the Bears and heavy public money already on Philadelphia -- a real, not-yet-closed gap, not just noise.
